dashboard.label: Isovalent + Tenable Demo
dashboard.description: Narrative demo: correlate Tenable Cloud Security posture findings with Isovalent runtime telemetry by cluster and workload. Example story — alex-aws-cluster has vulnerable coredns, kube-proxy, and aws-network-policy-agent images with matching process execution and security alerts.

search.query: index=cisco_security_cloud sourcetype=cisco:isovalent:* source=demo-tenable-correlation | eval cluster=coalesce(cluster, 'cluster-name') | stats count by cluster | append [ search index=tenable (source=Ermetic OR source=demo-tenable-correlation) type=Finding status=Open | rex field=resources{} "cluster/(?<cluster>[^/\"]+)" | rex field=resources{} ":cluster/(?<cluster>[^/\"]+)" | rex field=resourceNames{} "^(?<cluster>[^|]+)" | rex field=description "(?i)EKS Cluster (?<cluster>[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*)" | rex field=description "^(?<cluster>[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*)" | where isnotnull(cluster) | stats count by cluster ] | stats sum(count) as events by cluster | where events>0 | sort cluster | fields cluster

div.p: Tenable Cloud Security identifies vulnerable container images and misconfigurations. Isovalent observes what is actually running — process execution, network connections, and security alerts. Select a cluster to walk through the correlation.

Demo tip: try alex-aws-cluster — Tenable reports vulnerable coredns (3 Critical CVEs) and kube-proxy images; Isovalent shows active processes and a Suspicious Download and Execute alert on the same workloads. The image-match pie chart includes no match slices for workloads where runtime drifted (e.g. aws-network-policy-agent repo path change, or eks-pod-identity-agent pulled from Public ECR).

panel.title: Step 1 — Posture: Open Findings by Workload

search.query: index=tenable (source=Ermetic OR source=demo-tenable-correlation) type=Finding status=Open | rex field=resources{} "cluster/(?<cluster_path>[^/\"]+)" | rex field=resources "cluster/(?<cluster_path2>[^/\"]+)" | rex field=resources{} ":cluster/(?<cluster_arn>[^/\"]+)" | rex field=resources ":cluster/(?<cluster_arn2>[^/\"]+)" | rex field=resourceNames{} "^(?<cluster_name>[^|]+)" | rex field=resourceNames "^(?<cluster_name2>[^|]+)" | rex field=description "(?i)EKS Cluster (?<cluster_desc>[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*)" | rex field=description "^(?<cluster_desc2>[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*)" | rex field=description "(?i)^(?<namespace_desc>[^|]+)\s*\|\s*(?<workload_desc>[^ ]+)" | rex field=description "(?i)(?<workload_img>eks-pod-identity-agent|kube-proxy|coredns|aws-network-policy-agent)" | rex field=description "container image stored in (?<container_image>[^,\s]+)" | eval cluster=coalesce(cluster_path, cluster_path2, cluster_arn, cluster_arn2, cluster_name, cluster_name2, cluster_desc, cluster_desc2) | eval namespace=trim(coalesce(namespace_desc, "kube-system")) | eval workload=coalesce(workload_desc, workload_img, "(cluster-level)") | where isnotnull(cluster) | where if("$cluster$"="*", 1=1, cluster="$cluster$") | dedup id | eval severity_order=case(severity="Critical",1, severity="High",2, severity="Medium",3, severity="Low",4, true(), 5) | sort severity_order workload | table cluster workload namespace severity title container_image description link
